Subject: CareWell discovery — throughput & fidelity playbook + next steps

Hi James / Priya —

Thanks again for the discovery earlier today. Quick recap + recommended evaluation plan so we can get you a short pilot that answers the core question: can we hit your latency/throughput targets while keeping extractive/clinical-fidelity within acceptable bounds.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Goal: document understanding + structured extraction for post-visit summaries. Target p95 latency < 150ms for short queries (<= 256 tokens), peak concurrent workload ~600–1,000 QPS during batch windows.
- Quality sensitivity: a small number of extraction edge-cases (medications, dosage, allergies) are critical — these will be our fidelity gates.
- Security: customer data stays in Redwood Dedicated pilot (no external logging).

Model candidates we recommend for the initial pilot (diverse size / instruction tuning):
- Llama2-70B (fp16 baseline) — highest quality baseline for extraction tests.
- OpenLlama-3-33B (AWQ 4-bit variant) — strong throughput wins, watch prompt-sensitive fidelity.
- Mistral-Instruct-22B (fp16 / small-quant runs) — good middle-ground for cost/quality.

Quant/config experiments to include in the pilot:
- AWQ 4-bit: expected large throughput wins on our serving runtime (continuous batching + smaller KV cache footprint). Good for lower-latency scenarios but can introduce small hallucination/formatting regressions on edge prompts.
- GPTQ 4-bit: generally better fidelity preservation vs AWQ, slightly less speedup. Strong option when fidelity gates are tight.
- FP8 (hardware/driver dependent): moderate speedups, conservative quality impact; treat as safety-tier.

Deliverables attached / links:
- carewell_benchmarks_080826.csv (what we'll collect during the PoC) [Attachment]
- carewell_promptset_v1.yaml (seed prompt sets: extraction, safety-sensitive, open-ended) [Attachment]
- Benchmark dashboard: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/carewell-080826

Proposed mutual action plan (2-week tactical PoC):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize pilot scope & sign technical addendum (owner: James / Neha) — target: 08/19
2) Week 1: Redwood runs three model variants (fp16 baseline, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4) against promptset_v1 and the dataset in the CSV. We produce a scoreboard (latency, p95, token cost, fidelity deltas). (owner: Redwood)
3) Week 2: Joint review, prioritize any failure-mode prompts and iterate quant/profile. Decide on rollout (Dedicated config or keep fp16). (owner: CareWell + Redwood)

Next step: can we lock a 45-minute technical deep-dive next Tuesday (08/18) with your ML/infra folks so Ben (our ML SE) can walk through benchmark config and expected tradeoffs?

Thanks — I attached an MVP map (mvp_map_carewell.xlsx) that maps the three pilot workloads to success gates.

Regards,

James / Priya —

Answers inline to your bullets + quick pilot pricing estimate.

1) Throughput / latency (directional, measured on our Dedicated 8x A100-like pool with continuous batching and standard KV cache):
- fp16 baseline (Llama2-70B): p50 ~ 85ms, p95 ~ 210–260ms for short queries at small batch sizes (1–4) — high quality, higher token cost.
- AWQ-4 (OpenLlama-3-33B, tuned AWQ kernel): typically 1.8–2.4x latency improvement over fp16 on identical hardware and 40–60% reduction in token compute cost. Expect p95 to move into the ~90–140ms range for short queries depending on batching.
- GPTQ-4 (33B class): closer fidelity to fp16 (see fidelity bullets) with 1.4–1.7x latency improvement and ~30–45% token compute reduction; p95 typically ~120–170ms.
- FP8 (experimental): modest improvements vs fp16 (1.2x) with the best stability when driver/kernel support is consistent — treat as fallback.

2) Fidelity (extraction accuracy on our seed promptset):
- On our clinical extraction eval (1000 seed examples):
  - fp16 baseline: Reference accuracy (we use F1 / entity extraction).
  - GPTQ-4: median delta ~ -0.5% to -1.2% F1 vs fp16 (very constrained degradation; often indistinguishable on majority of prompts).
  - AWQ-4: median delta ~ -1.5% to -3.2% F1; failure modes are concentrated on formatting/edge-case extraction (e.g., abbreviated dosage strings, nested lists).
  - FP8: delta typically in the -0.4% to -1.8% range but higher variance across drivers.

Notes: these ranges are workload-dependent — open-ended summarization shows larger deltas, extraction tasks are more robust. We'll provide the detailed per-prompt breakdown in the scoreboard.

3) Cost (two-week pilot, Dedicated reserved short-term usage estimate):
- Rough pilot compute booking: 4x 80GB GPUs (reserved for 2 weeks) + storage/ingest. Ballpark: $35–45k for the two-week dedicated pilot depending on burst capacity and data ingress. We can compress this with sample-sampling if you want a lighter, single-week proof-of-concept.

Recommended immediate next steps:
- Confirm scope (full 2-week vs 1-week sample).
- Share any internal seed dataset (if you prefer not to send PHI, use synthetic or redacted CSV rows).
- Schedule the technical deep-dive 08/18 11:00am PT (Ben will demo benchmark config).

Ben — can you attach the quick-run commands and an example scoreboard snippet we can share in the deep-dive?

Thanks — I’ll update the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CARE-2026-09

James / Priya —

Quick technical notes ahead of Tuesday's deep-dive. Numbers below are practical ballparks based on our internal 33B/70B runs and the pilot config Neha outlined.

Benchmark context: short-query = <=256 tokens; continuous batching enabled (latency SLOs applied), KV cache warm.

AWQ-4 (OpenLlama-3-33B)
- Throughput: single 80GB GPU with continuous batching: ~700–1,200 inferences/minute for short queries depending on batch-size and request packing. On our Dedicated pool with the autoscaler configured for your target bursts, expect the p95 ~90–140ms.
- Fidelity caveat: AWQ changes token-level distributions in some kernels — we see structured-extraction format shifts (e.g., missing trailing punctuation that some regexes rely on). Mitigations: post-processing normalization or small prompt-engineering fixes; we can also exclude AWQ for a small set of golden prompts.

GPTQ-4
- Throughput: smaller win vs AWQ; expect ~1.4x improvement vs fp16. Better fidelity preservation; more predictable regressions.
- Operational: GPTQ packages are more straightforward to integrate into our kernel selection path; less custom kernel work.

FP8
- Throughput: modest uplift vs fp16; stable if runtime + drivers are consistent.
- Risk: hardware/driver combos matter — we recommend FP8 only after we validate the Dedicated stack drivers.

Practical experiment matrix (what I'll run for the PoC):
- Models: OpenLlama-3-33B (fp16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4), Llama2-70B (fp16 baseline), Mistral-Instruct-22B (fp16).
- Prompt sets: carewell_promptset_v1.yaml (extraction / safety / open-ended).
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tail-token-cost (tokens/sec), extraction F1 (per-entity), top-3 hallucination counts.
- Ops knobs: batch packing thresholds (1/4/8/16), KV cache window sizes (0/64/128), aggressive prefix caching for repeated templates.

Quick commands (attachment: quant_experiment_commands.sh) show the exact run calls (model variant + quant artifact + bench config). I'll also drop a scoreboard CSV with our seeded runs into the shared Drive before the call.

If you want, we can run an initial 24–48hr smoke run on a small sample before the official PoC to sanity-check AWQ kernels on your most critical prompts.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
